title: Uniform provisions concerning the approval of vehicles with regard to their equipment which may include: a temporary use spare unit, run flat tyres and/or a run flat system, and/or extended mobility tyres (version 3.1.0, 03 series of amendments)
scope_summary: Approves M1 and N1 vehicle types with regard to their equipment with a temporary-use spare unit, run-flat tyres or a run-flat system, and/or extended mobility tyres, including where applicable a run-flat warning system. Run-flat tyres, run-flat systems and extended mobility tyres used totally deflated are treated as temporary-use spare units (Type 5).
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to the approval of vehicles of category M1 and N1 when equipped with: (a) A temporary use spare unit; and/or (b) Run-flat tyres and/or a run-flat system; and/or (c) Extended mobility tyres. For the purposes of this Regulation, spare wheel and tyre substitute units in the form of run-flat tyres or a run-flat system or extended mobility tyres in a totally deflated condition, are to be treated as being temporary-use spare units as defined in paragraph 2.10. of this Regulation.
applies_to_components: Temporary-use spare unit (wheel and tyre assembly differing from the standard spare unit)
Spare wheel with different offset or size designation
relation_to_other_regulations: Refers to UN Regulation No. 30 for precise definitions of tyre size designation features and tyre structure (bias ply, bias-belted, radial ply, run-flat).
Refers to the Consolidated Resolution R.E.3 (ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.4) for the definition of vehicle categories M1 and N1 and for distinguishing numbers of Contracting Parties.
Approval numbers currently begin with 03 (03 series of amendments); paragraph 12 contains transitional provisions relative to earlier series.

defined_terms.label: Approval of a vehicle
defined_terms.definition: The approval of a vehicle type with regard to its temporary-use spare wheel and tyre unit.

defined_terms.label: Vehicle type with regard to its temporary-use spare unit
defined_terms.definition: Vehicles not differing in maximum axle loads, spare unit characteristics, method of drive, suspension, braking system, wheel/tyre size and wheel offset.

defined_terms.label: Wheel
defined_terms.definition: A complete wheel consisting of a rim and a wheel disc.

defined_terms.label: Wheel size designation
defined_terms.definition: A designation comprising at least the nominal rim diameter, the nominal rim width and the rim profile.

defined_terms.label: Wheel offset
defined_terms.definition: The distance from the hub abutment face to the centre line of the rim.

defined_terms.label: Tyre
defined_terms.definition: A pneumatic tyre forming, with its wheel, a continuous essentially toroidal closed chamber containing gas (or gas and liquid) normally used above atmospheric pressure.

defined_terms.label: Normal tyre
defined_terms.definition: A tyre suitable for all normal, on-road, conditions of use.

defined_terms.label: Temporary-use spare tyre
defined_terms.definition: A tyre specifically designed to differ from a normal tyre and intended only for temporary use under restricted driving conditions.

defined_terms.label: Run-flat tyre / Self supporting tyre
defined_terms.definition: A pneumatic tyre structure (e.g. reinforced sidewalls) that, on the appropriate wheel and without supplementary components, provides basic tyre functions at least at 80 km/h for 80 km in flat tyre running mode.

defined_terms.label: Run-flat system / Extended mobility system
defined_terms.definition: An assembly of functionally dependent components including a tyre that together provide basic tyre functions at least at 80 km/h for 80 km in flat tyre running mode.

defined_terms.label: Extended Mobility Tyre
defined_terms.definition: A pneumatic radial tyre designed to operate inflated and, without supplementary components, to provide basic tyre functions at 80 km/h for 80 km in flat tyre running mode.

defined_terms.label: Flat tyre running mode
defined_terms.definition: The state of a tyre essentially maintaining structural integrity while operating at an inflation pressure between 0 and 70 kPa.

defined_terms.label: Basic tyre function
defined_terms.definition: The normal capability of an inflated tyre to support a given load up to a given speed and transmit driving, steering and braking forces to the ground.

defined_terms.label: Tyre size designation
defined_terms.definition: A combination of figures uniquely identifying tyre geometric size: nominal section width, nominal aspect ratio and nominal diameter.

defined_terms.label: Tyre structure
defined_terms.definition: The technical characteristics of the tyre carcass: bias ply, bias-belted, radial ply or run-flat.

defined_terms.label: Standard spare unit
defined_terms.definition: A wheel and tyre assembly identical in size designations, wheel offset and tyre structure to that fitted in the same axle position for normal operation (wheel material and fixings may differ).

defined_terms.label: Temporary-use spare unit
defined_terms.definition: Any wheel and tyre assembly that is not a standard spare unit, of Types 1 to 5.

defined_terms.label: Maximum mass
defined_terms.definition: The maximum vehicle mass stated by the manufacturer to be technically permissible.

defined_terms.label: Maximum axle load
defined_terms.definition: The manufacturer-indicated maximum total vertical force between the tyres of one axle and the ground.

defined_terms.label: Run-Flat Warning System
defined_terms.definition: A system which delivers information to the driver that a tyre is operating in the flat tyre running mode.

classes_and_variants.name: Temporary-use spare unit Type 1
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: The tyre is a temporary-use spare tyre (para 2.4.2).

classes_and_variants.name: Temporary-use spare unit Type 2
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: The wheel has a different offset from the wheel fitted in the same axle position for normal operation.

classes_and_variants.name: Temporary-use spare unit Type 3
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: The tyre is of a different structure from that fitted in the same axle position for normal operation.

classes_and_variants.name: Temporary-use spare unit Type 4
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: A normal tyre, but the wheel and/or tyre size designation differs from that fitted in the same axle position for normal operation.

classes_and_variants.name: Temporary-use spare unit Type 5
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: A run-flat tyre, run-flat system or extended mobility tyre fitted for normal long-term use but used in an emergency totally deflated.

classes_and_variants.name: Standard spare unit (outside scope of temporary-use requirements)
classes_and_variants.distinguished_by: Identical wheel/tyre size designations, offset and tyre structure to the normal-operation unit.

applicability_hints: Any spare wheel/tyre assembly on an M1/N1 vehicle that differs from the normal-use wheel/tyre in tyre type, wheel offset, tyre structure or wheel/tyre size designation is a temporary-use spare unit (Types 1-4) and brings the vehicle under R64.

A space-saver/compact spare, or a full-size spare with a different offset or size, triggers R64; a spare identical except for wheel material (steel vs alloy) and fixing nuts/bolts is a standard spare unit and does not.

Fitting run-flat (self-supporting) tyres, extended mobility tyres or a run-flat system (e.g. tyre plus support insert) as original equipment brings the vehicle under R64 as Type 5 temporary-use spare unit.
Vehicles with run-flat tyres/systems require a run-flat warning system informing the driver of flat tyre running mode; telltales/ECUs providing this function are relevant to R64 approval.
R64 approves the vehicle, not the tyre itself; tyre component approval (including run-flat and temporary-use spare tyres) is under UN R30, which R64 references for size and structure definitions.
Changes to suspension, braking system, drive configuration, axle loads, wheel offset or wheel/tyre size may create a new vehicle type under R64 and require re-testing of braking/deviation.
General tyre pressure monitoring (TPMS) is not part of this 03-series version; it is addressed under UN R141.
